selected_findings.suggested_fix: Tie unauthorized notifications to the auth session that started each request. Increment a session epoch on login and logout; capture it when a rental request starts, and dispatch session-expired only if the epoch still matches when the 401 arrives. Verify with a delayed old-session 401 returned after a fresh login.
selected_findings.title: Late unauthorized response can expire a new login
selected_findings.why_it_matters: A rental request started under an old session can return 401 after the user logs out and logs in again. Its unconditional global event then clears the newly authenticated user and redirects back to login. The route cleanup aborts list/get reads, but create/update/delete requests do not accept a signal and can still finish late.

selected_findings.title: Cancel leaves an in-flight write running
selected_findings.why_it_matters: After submitting a create, update, or delete, the user can click Cancel while the request is still pending. The form unmounts, but the server write continues. Home can load before that write finishes, showing stale listings; a later write can complete without any success notice. For delete, a listing can disappear after the user chose Cancel.

Constructed sequence: hold a POST or DELETE before commit, click the still-active Cancel link, let Home's GET return the old list, then let the write finish successfully. The mounted guard suppresses the only completion action and the new Home receives no invalidation, leaving the old list rendered. The same sequence is reachable through App.jsx:97-99's Home navigation.

The effect at Home.jsx:12-25 requests the list on Home mount; neither query nor attempt changes when a mutation from the unmounted form later succeeds. A delayed request can therefore commit after that list response with no subsequent refresh.
selected_findings.first_evidence: frontend/src/components/forms.jsx:62 -- if (mounted.current) navigate("/", { state: { notice: successMessage } });
selected_findings.suggested_fix: Have successful rental create/update/delete callbacks publish a shared rental revision or rentals-changed event, and have Home refetch when that revision/event changes even if the submitting form has unmounted. Retain the mounted guard for form state and navigation. Disable or relabel Cancel while pending so it does not imply that an already-issued write will be canceled. Verify by delaying a mutation until after navigation to Home and its initial list response, then resolving the mutation and checking that Home refreshes.
selected_findings.title: Leaving a pending mutation keeps Home stale
selected_findings.why_it_matters: If a user submits a slow create or delete and clicks Cancel or Home while it is saving, Home can fetch the list before the write commits. The successful mutation then does nothing because the form has unmounted, and Home has no mutation-completion subscription, so a created listing stays missing or a deleted listing remains visible until another refresh. Publishing successful rental mutations independently of the form lifetime lets the mounted Home reload the actual saved data without navigating the user away from their current screen.

selected_findings.title: Cover invalid create input and failed-load retry paths
selected_findings.why_it_matters: The mock browser suite verifies valid submissions, server 422 errors and mutation network rejection but never exercises invalid client input or failures during the session/list reads. selected_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the article wait from expiryFlow and wait for the home page to finish its listing fetch (for example, a GET /api/rentals response or result-count/empty state) before starting the idle delay. Then run the expiry test against an otherwise empty database.
selected_findings.title: Expiry check fails when the database is empty
selected_findings.why_it_matters: The real suite creates and deletes its own listing before the expiry suite runs. If the database has no other listings, login succeeds and the home page loads, but this unrelated article assertion times out before the idle-expiry behavior is tested. The runtime guard then reports a failed expiry check for a valid empty database.

evidence: Browser Popen likewise uses start_new_session=True at tests/browser_hw04_part1_runtime.py:120 and :150; group cleanup is reached only in finally at lines 159-169, with no SIGTERM handler in the runner.
selected_findings.suggested_fix: Install a SIGTERM handler before launching owned subprocesses that raises a controlled termination exception or sets a cancellation flag, so Python executes the existing finally cleanup. Verify by signaling the runner during a waiting checkpoint and checking that its child process groups and listening port are gone.
selected_findings.title: Terminate owned processes when runner receives SIGTERM
selected_findings.why_it_matters: The runner starts the server and browsers in independent sessions. A SIGTERM sent to the runner, as by a job timeout or cancellation, terminates Python without executing its finally block, leaving the owned server or browser running and the port occupied. The existing group cleanup covers Python exceptions and normal exit only.
